sentences.text: Maintenance begins only after the work scope, access route, and responsible supervisor have been confirmed for the shift.
The Duty Planner checks that the planned task matches the approved work authorization and that required personnel and equipment are available.
The Work Permit Portal produces the Isolation Boundary Sketch.
The Field Supervisor reviews the worksite limits with the crew before anyone enters the controlled area.
Physical boundaries are marked so that the work area and any adjacent operating equipment are clearly distinguishable.
The crew confirms that the marked limits match the current isolation points and the approved maintenance scope.
The Electrical Technician verifies electrical isolation at the work location before work on electrical equipment begins.
The Substation Operator confirms that switching conditions affecting the worksite are understood by the relevant personnel.
The Vessel Master confirms that the vessel is safely positioned and that transfer conditions remain acceptable.
The Marine Coordinator suspends access when sea or weather conditions make transfer unsafe.
A Weather Hold remains in effect until the responsible operational authority confirms that conditions permit work to proceed.
Personnel use the North Access Scanner or South Access Scanner at the designated entry point.
The Personnel Tracking Console is checked to confirm that people entering and leaving the site are accounted for.
The Field Supervisor verifies each worker's authorization, competence, and fitness for the assigned task.
Before starting, the crew inspects personal protective equipment, communications equipment, and rescue equipment for serviceability.
The HSE Officer checks that emergency routes, muster points, and rescue arrangements are understood by everyone at the worksite.
The crew tests the required radio channel with the Operations Radio Console before separating into work teams.
Tools and loose materials are secured against dropped-object hazards and movement caused by vessel motion.
Access to the worksite is restricted to personnel listed for the task, and visitors remain under escort.
The Field Supervisor pauses the job if actual conditions differ from the approved method or the marked worksite boundaries.
Any change to the work scope requires a renewed safety review before affected work resumes.
The crew maintains clear access to fire equipment, escape routes, and lifting areas throughout the task.
At shift handover, the outgoing supervisor briefs the incoming supervisor on site conditions, access status, and outstanding hazards.
Work is closed out only after personnel are accounted for, equipment is removed or secured, and the worksite is left in a safe condition.
